title: Pump strainer, suction valves and the vacuum route
audience: Pool service technicians who open pump strainers and set suction valves on home pools
learningOutcomes: Open and close a pump strainer in the correct order without drawing air into the system
Set the the valves on the intake side for normal circulation and for vacuuming
Explain the risk from a blocked suction fitting and the supervision rule that follows
Stop the pump, then isolate power before any work on the pump or its motor

instruction.heading: The job of the pump strainer
instruction.body: The strainer basket sits ahead of the pump together with stops debris before it reaches the impeller, where it could cause damage. The UK handbook makes that point. To open the strainer, release the lid's screw thread or clamp and lift the lid off. First close the suction valves ahead of the pump together with set the multiport valve, so that water in the pipework does not drain back out. Reopen the valves after the lid goes back on. Check the lid seal and the O-ring. A worn seal lets air into the pump, which lowers the flow and makes priming harder.

instruction.heading: Valve positions at the intake
instruction.body: Most installations fit a small group of valves on the intake side. One serves the skimmer line and another the main drain. With normal circulation both ought to be fully open. When vacuuming via the skimmer, open the skimmer valve fully and close the main drain valve. A separate vacuum point has its own valve, and that valve is set to suit the route in use. Balance the flow by opening the valves gradually until the straining sound from the pump stops. Never start the pump with the valves in a position you have not checked.

instruction.heading: Blocked suction outlets
instruction.body: A blocked suction fitting can cause serious or fatal drowning. A suction outlet can hold a person firmly, so a blocked outlet is an entrapment risk. The product manual says young children who use pool equipment need a responsible adult watching them at all times, and must not use the product only when they are under constant adult supervision. Before a swim, confirm that the outlets and the strainer are clear, and refer any cracked or missing outlet cover to the owner or operator. Do not fit or remove an outlet cover unless the owner has given written instruction and supplied the correct part.

instruction.heading: Isolating power before pump work
instruction.body: Keep hands off the pump whenever it is energised or still connected to power. Dangerous voltage can cause serious or fatal injury. Switch the pump off at its isolator, confirm the supply is dead, and only then open the strainer or the motor housing. Motor servicing belongs to a motor service centre. The handbook notes that if a motor refuses to start, the fuse should be checked, and that a humming motor may have a jammed impeller. In that case, cut the power supply and contact the maintenance company. Electrical work itself is covered in “Electrical connection, bonding and motor safety for a pool pump”.

instruction.heading: Recording the valve settings
instruction.body: Note the position of every valve before you change anything, so that the system can be restored to its normal state. A valve left in the wrong setting is a common reason for weak flow, and the fault often goes unnoticed until the next visit. Record the strainer condition, the state of the lid seal, the valve settings and the gauge reading when you finish.

procedure: Record the current valve positions and the gauge reading.
Stop the pump at its isolator, and confirm it is off before you touch the strainer lid.
Close the valves that sit ahead of the pump plus set the multiport valve as the manual directs.
Open the strainer lid, lift out the basket, and clear the debris.
Check the lid seal and O-ring, clean the lid and basket seat, and replace any damaged part.
Return the basket, seat the lid and tighten the clamp evenly. Open the suction valves again.
Set the skimmer and main drain valves to the position for normal circulation or the vacuum route in use.
Start the pump, confirm steady flow and a steady gauge reading, and record the result.

workedExamples.situation: The gauge reads low and the water in the skimmer appears still. The owner says the pump is fine because it 'sounds normal'.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop the pump at its isolator and check the strainer basket, the lid seal and the suction valve positions. Note the valve positions and the basket condition, then clear any blockage and restore the valves. Record the readings before and after. If the flow is still low, refer it. Sound alone does not show that the flow is correct.

workedExamples.situation: A child is playing near the suction outlet at the shallow end and the outlet cover is cracked.
workedExamples.reasoning: Ask a responsible adult to take charge of the child and move the child away from the outlet. Stop any work on the outlet. Record the cracked cover, the time and the action taken, and refer the cover to the owner or operator for replacement. Do not fit a replacement cover yourself without the owner's written instruction.

equipmentAndPpe: Strainer lid O-ring and spare seal as supplied for the model
Gloves for debris and wet parts
Torch for checking the basket and outlet covers
Isolator access and a lock or tag if the site requires one
Record sheet for valve positions and gauge readings

commonErrors.error: Opening the strainer lid with the suction valves still open
commonErrors.prevention: Close the suction valves first and confirm the pump is off.

commonErrors.error: Leaving a valve in an unrecorded position
commonErrors.prevention: Record the valve positions before and after every change.

commonErrors.error: Reading a normal sound as proof of correct flow
commonErrors.prevention: Check the gauge, the basket and the valve positions as well.

commonErrors.error: Working on the motor while power is connected
commonErrors.prevention: Isolate and confirm the supply is off before any motor or pump work.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: A blocked suction fitting can lead to serious or fatal injury through drowning. Young children using pool equipment need a responsible adult watching at all times, and must not use the product only if they are watched constantly by an adult.
Never work on the pump while it remains running or while power remains connected. Dangerous voltage can cause serious or fatal injury.
Avoid using the strainer lid or valves as a step or support. Damaged lids and seals must be replaced before the pump is started.
Motor servicing is for a motor service centre. Do not open or repair the motor.
Disconnect and refit electrical connections only if you are trained to do so. Otherwise ask the contractor to fit a suitable outdoor-rated plug or connector.
Electrical isolation, wiring and motor work need the licence described in “Electrical connection, bonding and motor safety for a pool pump”. This lesson does not grant that licence.

qualityStandard: Valve positions are recorded before and after every change.
The strainer lid is closed with a sound seal and the suction valves are open before the pump runs.
Any cracked or missing suction outlet cover is referred and recorded.
documentationEvidence: Record of valve positions and gauge readings before and after
Strainer condition and any part replaced
Referral note for suction outlet covers or motor concerns
summary: Close the suction valves before opening the strainer and open them again before the pump runs.
Blocked or uncovered suction outlets are a drowning risk and need supervision and referral.
Isolate and confirm power is off before any pump or motor work.

knowledgeChecks.question: Before a pump strainer lid is opened, what should be done first?
options: Set the filter to the waste position while the pump operates
Open the skimmer valve fully to clear debris
Fill the strainer with cleaning solution
Confirm the suction valves are closed and the pump is off

knowledgeChecks.question: A suction outlet cover is cracked. What is the correct response?
options: Ask an adult to take charge of nearby children, stop work on the outlet, and refer the cover
Fit a replacement cover yourself, using a spare from the store and then test the outlet
Use the outlet while the cover is cracked, since the pump still works and no one is watching
Remove the cover completely so that the flow is improved and leave the outlet open

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is the pump power isolated before the motor is inspected?
options: The motor can only be read with the supply switched off and the gauge is read first
Dangerous voltage can cause serious or fatal injury while the unit is connected
The gauge will not register while the motor is connected and the readings are then wrong
The water temperature changes when the motor is connected and the pool gets warmer
